questions_and_answers.question_text: Does the marker le appear in the negative answer?
Which adverb is included in the negative of a sentence containing combined le?
What does the adverb hái mean?
Which negative is used to negate the aspect of completion?
To what may méiyou be shortened?
Write the Chinese for "She hasn't come yet."
Where does hái always come in relation to the verb?

answers.answer_text: It always precedes the verb, although not always directly — elements such as the negatives bù and méi may come between an adverb and a verb.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What happens to the "yet" in English translations?
What does méiyou mean, and what does it do?

answers.answer_text: It means "not have," and it is used to negate the aspect of completion — to say that a certain event did not take place.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give the negative of Tā lái ("is coming") and of Tā lái le ("has come").

answers.answer_text: Tā bù lái ("isn't coming") and Tā hái méi(you) lái ("hasn't come yet").

articles.text:
3. A: Nǐ àiren yě lái le ma?                Has your wife come too?
   B: Tā hái méi lái.                       She hasn't come yet.

Notes on No. 3

Negative of combined le: Compare these affirmative and negative forms:

affirmative     Tā  |            | lái     |     (is coming)
negative        Tā  | bù         | lái     |     (isn't coming)
affirmative     Tā  |            | lái le  |     (has come [now])
negative        Tā  | hái méi(you) | lái   |     (hasn't come [yet])

Notice that the marker le does not appear in the negative answer in the exchange.

Hái: The negative of a sentence containing combined le will include the adverb hái, "yet," as well as the negative méi(you). In English, the "yet" is frequently left out.

Like other adverbs such as yě, hái always precedes the verb, although not always directly. Elements such as the negatives bù and méi may come between an adverb and a verb.

Méiyou, "not have," is used to negate the aspect of completion; that is, to say that a certain event did not take place. Méiyou may be shortened to méi. Here are three possible negative answers to the question Tā lái le ma? "Has he come?"

Tā hái méiyou lái.        (He hasn't come yet.)
Tā hái méi lái.           (He hasn't come yet.)
Tā méi lái.               (He hasn't come.)
